title: NRS Harwell marks 80 Years of history and innovation
text:
Press release
NRS Harwell marks 80 Years of history and innovation
This year, Nuclear Restoration Services (NRS) is celebrating a remarkable milestone as the Harwell site marks its 80th anniversary.
From:
Nuclear Restoration Services
and
Nuclear Decommissioning Authority
Published:
24 August 2026
Eight decades of scientific achievement, innovation and expertise have helped shape the UK’s nuclear industry, advanced healthcare and energy technologies, and transformed Oxfordshire into a world-renowned centre for science and research.
Today, under the stewardship of NRS, part of the Nuclear Decommissioning Authority (NDA) group, Harwell continues to play a vital role in delivering safe, sustainable decommissioning while enabling future generations of scientific discovery and economic growth.
Since its establishment in 1946, Harwell has been at the heart of the UK’s scientific progress, evolving from its early role in atomic research to a modern hub for decommissioning expertise and technological advancement.
In its earliest years, Harwell was instrumental in laying the foundations for the UK’s civil nuclear industry. The site hosted some of the country’s first research reactors and laboratories, driving innovation that shaped national energy policy and scientific capability for decades to come.
Harwell became a leader in radiological safety, developing protocols and expertise that have influenced international best practice. This commitment to safety remains central to NRS Harwell’s operations today, underpinning every aspect of its work.
Beyond nuclear research, Harwell has supported projects in advanced fuels, fusion technology and sustainable energy solutions. Its contributions have helped position the UK as a global leader in next-generation energy systems.
The site has also played a vital role in healthcare and industry, pioneering radiopharmaceuticals and isotope production that have supported life-saving treatments and industrial applications worldwide.
Today, NRS Harwell leads the way in safe decommissioning, dismantling legacy facilities with precision and care on behalf of the NDA. Through decades of specialist expertise, the site continues to tackle some of the UK’s most complex nuclear challenges while creating opportunities for regeneration, innovation and economic growth.
So far, decommissioning work has successfully removed more than one million square feet of facility footprint, cleared 1.6 million square feet of land, and enabled 23 hectares to be delicensed and released for redevelopment. This work has helped pave the way for the internationally recognised Harwell Science and Innovation Campus, which today supports thousands of jobs and hundreds of organisations at the forefront of science, technology and research.
Harwell’s remarkable history has also recently been celebrated through a dedicated ITV Meridian mini-series, highlighting the site’s contribution to science, innovation and nuclear expertise over the past eight decades. The series provides a behind-the-scenes look at the people, projects and legacy that have shaped Harwell and is available to watch through ITV Meridian catch-up and on ITV’s YouTube channel.
Gary Reid, Site Director, said:
Harwell’s 80-year legacy is a testament to the dedication and expertise of everyone who has worked here.
From groundbreaking research to today’s focus on safe decommissioning and innovation, the site has always been at the forefront of progress. We’re proud of our history and excited about what the future holds.
For more information about NRS Harwell’s history and future ambitions, please visit the
NRS GOV page
.

title: EM on fisheries TCA Specialised Committee position (COM(2026)293)
text:
Page 1 of 4 
 
EXPLANATORY MEMORANDUM ON A UK/EU WITHDRAWAL AGREEMENT OR 
TRADE AND COOPERATION AGREEMENT GOVERNANCE DOCUMENT  
COM(2026) 293 Final  
PROPOSAL FOR A COUNCIL DECISION AMENDING COUNCIL DECISION 
2021/1765 OF 5 OCTOBER 2021 ON THE POSITION TO BE TAKEN ON BEHALF 
OF THE EUROPEAN UNION, FOR THE PERIOD 2021-2026, IN THE SPECIALISED 
COMMITTEE 
ON 
FISHERIES 
ESTABLISHED 
BY 
THE 
TRADE 
AND 
COOPERATION AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE EUROPEAN UNION AND THE 
EUROPEAN ATOMIC ENERGY COMMUNITY, OF THE ONE PART, AND THE 
UNITED KINGDOM OF GREAT BRITAIN AND NORTHERN IRELAND, OF THE 
OTHER PART 
Submitted by the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), 21 
August 2026 
 
SUBJECT MATTER 
 
1. Following the UK’s exit from the European Union (EU), the UK became an 
independent coastal State. The EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA) 
entered into force on 1 May 2021 and includes fisheries provisions. The TCA 
establishes the Specialised Committee on Fisheries (SCF), a forum for the EU and 
United Kingdom (UK) to discuss matters relating to fisheries management 
measures. 
 
2. Under Article 508(2) of the TCA, the SCF may adopt acts or measures, including 
decisions and recommendations relating to: 
a. recording matters agreed by the Parties following the annual fisheries 
consultations, where Total Allowable Catches (TACs) are discussed; 
b. fisheries management measures, including emergency measures and multi-
year strategies; 
c. amending the list of pre-existing international obligations referred to in Article 
496(2) of the TCA; 
d. on any other aspect of cooperation on sustainable fisheries management 
under the fisheries heading of the TCA; and 
e. on the modalities of a review under Article 510 of the TCA. 
 
3. Council Decision (EU) 2021/1765, made on 05 October 2021, laid out the EU’s 
objectives within the SCF, which include to: 
a. support the long-term sustainability of fisheries; 

Page 2 of 4 
 
b. manage fisheries in line with the EU’s Common Fisheries Policy to achieve 
the maximum sustainable yield for stocks; 
c. utilise the best available scientific advice particularly from the International 
Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES); 
d. promote an ecosystem approach to fisheries management; 
e. ensure adherence to and consistency with other international commitments, 
such as the United Nations Agreement on Straddling and Highly Migratory 
Fish Stocks (UNFSA). 
 
4. In 2023, the EU conducted a review to ensure that the consultations and the 
meetings carried out under the SCF appropriately reflected the objectives laid out 
in Council Decision (EU) 2021/1765. This review determined that no revision was 
necessary to Council Decision (EU) 2021/1765 and no implementation issues were 
identified.  
 
5. This proposal aims to extend the EU’s position within the SCF until 30 June 2038. 
Without this extension, Decision (EU) 2021/1765 was due to expire on the 31 
December 2026. 
 
6. This proposal is therefore primarily a procedural matter and does not represent a 
change in EU policy. Should the EU adopt this proposal, the EU’s policy will remain 
consistent with UK legislation, enabling collaborative working between the UK and 
EU in managing shared stocks as per the TCA. 
 
SCRUTINY HISTORY 
 
7. There is no Parliamentary scrutiny history relevant to this Explanatory 
Memorandum. 
 
MINISTERIAL RESPONSIBILITY 
 
8. Responsibility lies with the Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural 
Affairs. 
 
INTEREST OF THE DEVOLVED GOVERNMENTS (DGs) 
 
9. International fisheries negotiations is not a devolved matter, but the UK Government 
will continue to discuss matters where relevant with each of the DG. DGs have been 
consulted on the preparation of this explanatory memorandum and raised no 
concerns regarding the EU's proposal. 
 
LEGAL AND PROCEDURAL ISSUES 

Page 3 of 4 
 
 
10.  
 
i. Legal Base 
 
The EU’s legal basis for this decision is Article 43 Treaty on the Functioning of the 
European Union (TFEU), in conjunction with Article 218(9) TFEU.  
Procedural legal basis 
Article 218(9) of the TFEU provides for decisions establishing ‘the positions to be 
adopted on the Union’s behalf in a body set up by an agreement, when that body 
is called upon to adopt acts having legal effects, with the exception of acts 
supplementing or amending the institutional framework of the agreement.’ 
Article 8(1)(q) of the TCA establishes the SCF, Article 8(4) the areas of 
competence of the SCF generally and Article 508 lists, in a non-exhaustive 
manner, the tasks and areas of competence of the SCF specifically. 
Decisions adopted by the SCF are binding on the Parties to the TCA, in 
accordance with Article 10 of the TCA.  
Substantive legal basis 
The EU’s substantive legal basis for the proposed decision is based on Article 43 
TFEU, on the basis it falls within the EU’s common fisheries policy area. 
 
ii. Voting procedure 
 
The adoption of the Decision by the EU Council will be on the basis of qualified 
majority voting. 
 
iii. Timetable for adoption and implementation 
 
The Council decision will be adopted in due course. 
 
 
POLICY AND LEGAL IMPLICATIONS 
 
11. The UK Government’s policy is for the continuation of the SCF under its current 
structures. Should the EU accept COM(2026)293, it will be in alignment with the 
UK’s position. 
 
CONSULTATION 
 
12. No external consultation has been necessary on this matter. 

Page 4 of 4 
 
 
FINANCIAL IMPLICATIONS 
 
13. There are no financial implications for the UK. 
 
 
 
 
 
STEPHEN MORGAN MP 
PARLIAMENTARY UNDER- SECRETARY OF STATE 
DEPARTMENT FOR ENVIRONMENT, FOOD AND RURAL AFFAIRS

The Beacon Fen Energy Park DCO application has today been granted development consent by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero.
From:

Published:

Lackford Estate (representative of Beacon Fen Energy Park)
The project comprises a 400MW photovoltaic farm incorporating up to 600MVA Battery Energy Storage System and on-site substation and electrical connection, including solar PV panels; single stacked BESS units; security perimeter fencing; hedgerow improvements; ecological enhancements; above and/or below ground electrical cable connection at up to 400kV; associated development and ancillary works.
The application was submitted to the Planning Inspectorate for consideration by Beacon Fen Energy Park Limited on 08 April 2025 and accepted for examination on 01 May 2025.
Following an examination during which the public, statutory consultees and interested parties were given the opportunity to give evidence to the Examining Authority, recommendations were made to the Secretary of State on 22 May 2026.
This is the 112th energy application out of 180 applications examined to date and was again completed by the Planning Inspectorate within the statutory timescale laid down in the Planning Act 2008.
Local communities continue to be given the opportunity of being involved in the examination of projects that may affect them. Local people, the local authority and other interested parties were able to participate in this six-month examination.
The Examining Authority listened and gave full consideration to all local views and the evidence gathered during the examination before making its recommendation to the Secretary of State.
The decision, the recommendation made by the Examining Authority to the Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero and the evidence considered by the Examining Authority in reaching its recommendation are publicly available on the
project pages of the National Infrastructure Planning website.
This decision was made by Baroness Curran on behalf of the Energy Secretary’s legal authority.
